name: Jeonju
tagline: Korea's food capital and a city of 700 traditional hanok houses, where bibimbap, makgeolli and calligraphy have deep roots.
highlight: A bibimbap lunch in Jeonju Hanok Village, followed by a walk through tile-roofed lanes.
shortDescription: A UNESCO City of Gastronomy with a large hanok village, Gyeonggijeon Shrine, Nambu Market and Korea's best bibimbap, makgeolli and banquet-style side dishes.
metaDescription: A Jeonju travel guide: Jeonju Hanok Village, Gyeonggijeon Shrine, bibimbap, Nambu Market, makgeolli, Omokdae, where to stay, how to get there and a two-day plan.
nearestAirport: Incheon (ICN) or Gimpo (GMP), then about 2 hours by KTX or bus
goodFor: Food lovers, traditional culture, slow travel

image.alt: Tile-roofed hanok houses in Jeonju Hanok Village

intro: Jeonju is a city of about 650,000 in the fertile south-west, and it is widely regarded as the culinary heart of South Korea. UNESCO named it a Creative City of Gastronomy in 2012, and locals will tell you that a meal in Jeonju includes far more side dishes than anywhere else. It is the home of bibimbap, the rice bowl mixed with vegetables and chilli paste, and of a regional banquet tradition in which a table fills with small dishes as soon as you order drinks.

The old heart of the city is Jeonju Hanok Village, a district of about 700 traditional houses with curved tile roofs, alleys and courtyard cafés. It grew around the Gyeonggijeon Shrine, which holds a portrait of the founder of the Joseon dynasty, who was born in Jeonju's family line, and the area is the country's best place to try on hanbok and stroll through real streets rather than a museum set.

Jeonju is compact and easy: a day or two lets you eat, walk the village, browse the Nambu Market and taste the local makgeolli. It is about two hours from Seoul by KTX, and it fits between Seoul and the south-east, making it a natural stop on a longer trip.

whyVisit.intro: Jeonju offers food and tradition in one compact, walkable place.

points.text: The most famous bowl in Korea.

points.title: An easy stop

attractionsIntro: Everything worth seeing is within a short walk of the hanok village.

attractions.name: Jeonju Hanok Village

image.alt: A lane in Jeonju Hanok Village lined with tile-roofed houses

attractions.text: A district of about 700 hanok with cafés, workshops, guesthouses and hanbok rentals, and the main street for snacks.
attractions.tip: Stay overnight, when the crowds go.

attractions.name: Gyeonggijeon Shrine

image.alt: The Gyeonggijeon Shrine buildings in Jeonju

attractions.text: A shrine that houses a portrait of King Taejo, the founder of the Joseon dynasty, in a quiet compound.

attractions.name: Jeondong Cathedral
attractions.text: A Romanesque-Byzantine church from the early 1900s, in red brick, beside the hanok village.

attractions.name: Nambu Market
attractions.text: A traditional market with food stalls and a night market on weekends.

attractions.name: Omokdae
attractions.text: A pavilion on a hill with views across the hanok village's rooftops.

attractions.name: Korean Traditional Wine Museum
attractions.text: A museum where you can learn about and taste traditional wines.

thingsToDoIntro: Jeonju is about eating and strolling.

thingsToDo.title: Eat Jeonju bibimbap
thingsToDo.text: Try the classic bowl with raw beef and bean sprouts.

thingsToDo.title: Wear a hanbok
thingsToDo.text: Rent traditional dress and stroll the village.

thingsToDo.title: Drink makgeolli
thingsToDo.text: Visit a makgeolli alley for a kettle of rice wine with a table of dishes.

thingsToDo.title: Try a hanok stay
thingsToDo.text: Sleep on a heated floor in a traditional house.

thingsToDo.title: Snack along the street
thingsToDo.text: Choco pies, grilled skewers and egg bread.

foodIntro: Jeonju's food is a national point of pride, and a meal is generous.

foods.text: Bean sprout soup with rice, a cheap breakfast and hangover cure.

accommodation.intro: Stay in the hanok village for atmosphere.

gettingThere.intro: Jeonju is reached by KTX or bus from Seoul.

options.text: About two hours, by KTX to Jeonju station.
About three hours from Seoul Express Bus Terminal.
Via a bus or a change of train.
The village and market are close together.

bestTime.headline: April and October
bestTime.summary: Jeonju has four seasons, with hot summers and cold winters.
